method: SQLite check-in identifiers were located in the two branch timelines below; each identifier's info page supplied its commit date, comment, and containing release. Release dates and per-release sqlite3.c SHA3-256 digests come from the SQLite change log. Presence in a 3.53 branch timeline interval that ends at a release tag means the check-in is an ancestor of that release and of the later 3.53 branch release recorded here; other branches and later reversions were not checked.

check_ins.comment: Check for cells extending too far past the end of a page while searching an index.
Improved detection of corrupt freelist chains on btree pages, plus assert()s guarding the min-heap in PRAGMA integrity_check.

When rolling back a journal containing a super-journal pointer, only unlink the super-journal if the filename looks generated and the super-journal names the journal being rolled back. Limits crafted hot-journal file deletion.
When using a read-only WAL/SHM, handle a corrupt page size in the WAL file correctly.

When reading a super-journal name from a journal file, allocate a new buffer rather than using Pager.pTmpSpace. Prevents a buffer overrun with a VFS with large sqlite3_vfs.mxPathname and a small page size.
Ensure a hot journal is rolled back when a crash leaves a super-journal record whose magic and length are correct but whose name and checksum are both zeroed. Forum post 2026-07-20T18:27:00Z.
check_ins.supersedes_note: Corrects the September 9 readiness inference. The upstream forum report (https://sqlite.org/forum/info/2026-07-20T18:27:00Z) places the regression in 3.53.3 and excludes 3.53.2: the 3.53.3 refactor of readSuperJournal() introduced the empty-name path, while 3.53.2 pager_playback() tests zSuper[0]. The candidate 3.53.2 is not exposed to this regression.
